answer.read: Family foundry under margin pressure: part sits around or below full cost (Z price_stability, cost:310010 est. €132.64), it values cash strongly (asked for short payment, Z cash) and recognition of past concessions (Z recognition). Contract binding means price changes are only valid from the new year with notice (ctr:4600070110#3.1), and it accepted our notice-period point, yet its sheet still says November. It moved from €137.78 to €134.00 after our verified claims and accepted 14-day payment. It is open, not at final offer. Our alternative is dearer, so it holds leverage, but we have plenty of rounds left.
answer.message: Thank you for reviewing our data so carefully and for accepting the earlier payment terms. Since you agree on the contractual notice period, any new price can only start with the new calendar year, and our sheet reflects that. We value the long partnership with your family foundry and want it to stay healthy on this part. Our growing demand also means more work for your plant over the year ahead.
answer.reason: o2 has essentially the lowest C (€1,122,695, same as E0), but it fixes the date to the contractually valid 1 January, which the supplier has already conceded. That makes the counter coherent, where E0 repeats a November date we argued is invalid. Short payment meets its strong cash need. The price sits below the health price, which leaves room for later concessions in the relationship-charge zone without overshooting. The volume-growth argument speaks to its volume need without adding friction. Accepting €134 now would leave value on the table, given its pace of concessions.
